$comment: ADR 002 Task 1, revised 2026-09-02 under Amendments A-D. One row per pre-migration classes key, all 523 across 35 registry entries. No source changed.

amendments.A: Every name outside R2 cites a peer precedent or is marked NOVEL. Peer conventions absorbed 9 coinages: checkbox/radio/tracker/wrapper -> control (Ark), progress -> indicator, Loader indicator -> track+range (Ark Progress), connector -> separator (Ark Steps, already R2), heading -> header (Radix Accordion, already R2), initials -> fallback (Radix Avatar), mark -> marker (Ark Slider), tooltip -> valueText (Ark Slider), handle -> resizeHandle, presetButton -> presetTrigger (Ark DatePicker).
amendments.B: error + success collapse into `message` carrying data-state. Verified first: all 14 components that render a success message guard it with !error, so none can show both. R2's errorText and helperText are retired. The two-part exception is unused.
amendments.C: An absorbed key carrying structural utilities is promoted. 105 absorbed rows re-checked against splitLayers: 53 carried structural classes and were promoted with canonical names, 17 were R6 relocations to a child (access preserved), 52 remain absorbed.
amendments.D: Four R4 attribute values accepted: data-outside (Ark data-outside-range), data-range (Ark data-in-range; tri-value form ours), data-marked (NOVEL), `completed` for data-state (Ark Steps data-complete).

$comment_count: 57 amendment terms, up from 46 before the amendments and not down, because A and C pull opposite ways: A collapsed 9 coinages into peer names, C forced 53 previously-absorbed elements back into the vocabulary and 20 of them needed a name. 16 of the 57 now carry a peer precedent where none did before.

$correctedOn: 2026-09-02 (Task 3a): 24 rows carried outcome `unchanged` while naming a different target, so they were renames counted as no-ops. Corrected to `renamed` and the totals recomputed from the rows. key-migration.contract now asserts an `unchanged` row targets its own key, and that every total matches a count over the rows — neither was checked, which is why the drift survived.
$declaredMergesComment: Targets that more than one surviving key deliberately claims. A shared target not listed here is two elements fighting over one key. Every entry must also pass the structural test: the elements it merges may not have differing structural layers unless they are the same element (two keys on one className), which the contract detects from source.
$structuralBeforeComment: Structural layer of each key's default class string as it stood BEFORE Task 3a, read from git HEAD. R9's merge test asserts against this rather than the live constants: once the migration merges two keys the evidence is gone from the tree, and a gate that can no longer see its own evidence passes vacuously.
$coLocatedBeforeComment: Key pairs written into one className expression before Task 3a, i.e. two handles on ONE element. R9's merge test needs these to tell 'two keys on one element' (harmless) from 'two elements on one key' (the ADR 001 defect). Frozen from git HEAD for the same reason as structuralBefore: after the rename the old names are gone from the source and the check could no longer see its own evidence.
$task3bOutcome: 104 of the 108 planned deletions applied (97 state + 11 dead, minus 4 held back). Held back: CascadingDropdown.content — the dead list was re-derived post-3a and `menu` had taken that name, so it is a live key with 5 source references, not a dead one; DatePicker.dayFocused and DatePicker.dropdownItemSelected — blocked on the a11y phase, which is on the do-not-touch list, so the replacement state cannot be reached and the route cannot be proven; InternationalPhoneInput.countrySelectOptionSelected — its route is R6-nested and needs Task 4. Live keys are 384 against the table's predicted 369: the difference is those 4 plus the 12 R6-nested absorbs Task 3a deferred, whose keys still exist under their old names.
$task3bFindings: The replacement contract found six state rows whose `to` had gone stale under Amendment F (checkboxChecked -> itemControl in three components, labelWrapperBottom -> row, submenuItemSelected -> subItem, clockDisplayActive -> clockHours) and three states with no attribute on the element the surviving key styles (Switch's label had no data-disabled, both Stepper connectors had no data-orientation) — all fixed before deleting. CascadingDropdown.menuItemDisabled was the sixteenth key wrongly waived on this branch: its recorded reason said a disabled top-level option did not render it, but the fixture marked a disabled CHILD, not a top-level option.
